newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Firmer on tighter supplies.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Firmer on tighter supplies.

text.p: Singapore high sulphur fuel oil prices were firmer on Tuesday to reflect strong fuel oil swaps and SIMEX futures contract, traders said.
A 180-cst grade, 20,000-tonne cargo was heard sold by a major at $100 per tonne for May 29 and June 2 loading.
The 180-cst grade was traded at $98.50 per tonne last week.
"Sentiment is pretty firm and most people believe prices are in an uptrend," said one trader.
"But demand is not great. I think prices would stay supported and are not likely to shoot up," the trader added.
May fuel oil swaps edged up to $100.00/$101.00 from Monday's $99.00/$99.50 and June were at $98.50/$99.50 compared with $96.75/97.50.
Sentiment was also supported by anticipated tighter suppliers from the Middle East and South Korea, traders said.
Summer demand in the Middle East and turnarounds in South Korea, leading to fewer exports, have been expected to tighten supplies, they said.
On SIMEX fuel oil futures contract on late Tuesday, sentiment was also firm with June contract moving $1.00 up to $99.50 and July inching 40 cents up also to $98.40.
On Wednesday, Taiwan's Chinese Petroleum Corp will close a tender for two 0.5-percent, 38,000-tonne cargoes for June delivery.
Traders expected the result to shed some fresh direction for the market.
